result.summary: This agreement presents significant risk to High Speed Net Solutions (HSNS) as an Enterprise Buyer. High Speed Net Solutions is required to broadly indemnify E.piphany, while E.piphany's IP indemnity is heavily restricted and liability capped to initial term fees. Crucially, the contract lacks termination for convenience, deems deliverables accepted automatically after 10 days, and grants E.piphany sole ownership over all deliverables.

categoryScores.comment: R-INDEM-01 Fail: The indemnity structure is heavily biased, forcing Customer to provide broad indemnification while Vendor limits its IP indemnification to US IP and excludes liabilities for combinations or modifications.
R-LIAB-01 Fail: The liability cap applies strictly to E.piphany while excluding direct liabilities, and fails to provide standard uncapped exceptions for indemnity, confidentiality, or data breaches.
R-TERM-01 Fail: The contract only permits termination for cause or insolvency, lacking a provision for Customer to terminate for convenience with 30 days written notice.
R-IP-01 Fail: Vendor retains ownership over all deliverables created under the agreement, granting Customer only a non-exclusive license.
R-PRIV-01 Not Addressed: The provided contract excerpts contain no security standards or data breach notification timeframe.
R-PAY-01 Fail: Deliverables are automatically deemed accepted after 10 days if not formally rejected, which is overly restrictive compared to Net 45 and standard acceptance workflow.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Advocates for the Vendor (E.piphany), securing maximum IP retention, broad customer indemnification, liability limitations, and automatic acceptance periods.
agentPerspectives.stance: Aggressive protective stance favoring Vendor dominance.
keyPoints: Ensures all deliverable IP rights and software modifications remain strictly with E.piphany.
Imposes asymmetrical liability limits that shield E.piphany while placing broad indemnification burdens onto HSNS for its Outsourcing Services.
Uses short 10-day deemed acceptance periods to force swift customer acceptance and payment lock-in.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Reject all customer ownership requests over software deliverables; insist that all modifications belong exclusively to E.piphany.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on reaching a balanced deal that enables partnership execution while mitigating extreme commercial roadblocks.
agentPerspectives.stance: Pragmatic compromise to facilitate business operations.
keyPoints: Accepts E.piphany's core background IP ownership while insisting on a broader non-exclusive perpetual license for HSNS.
Proposes extending the deliverable review period from 10 days to 30 days to align with realistic technical operational cycles.
Softens the indemnification language to establish a mutual indemnification standard for core operational breaches.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Offer a mutual limitation of liability cap equal to 12 months of contract fees and extend deliverable acceptance review to 30 days.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Enforces strict adherence to Enterprise Buyer playbook rules, identifying critical compliance breaches and liability exposures.
agentPerspectives.stance: Strict risk mitigation and contractual compliance.
keyPoints: Failed R-INDEM-01 due to one-sided customer indemnification in Section 10.2 and restricted vendor IP indemnity in Section 10.1.
Failed R-LIAB-01 due to unilateral limitation of liability favoring vendor in Section 11 without standard uncapped exclusions.
Failed R-TERM-01, R-IP-01, and R-PAY-01 due to lack of termination for convenience, vendor deliverable ownership, and 10-day deemed acceptance.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Require immediate restructuring of Sections 6.4, 10, 11, and 12 to add mutual liability caps, 30-day convenience termination, 24-hour breach notice, and Customer deliverable rights.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners (each, an "Indemnified Party") against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities
redlines.proposedText: Each party agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its officers, directors, and employees from and against any third-party claims arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of intellectual property obligations under this Agreement.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany argues HSNS controls customer delivery and should bear all operational liabilities.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Unilateral customer indemnity leaves HSNS exposed to full operational liability while receiving zero third-party IP defense from the vendor.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Indemnification must be mutual and cover third-party IP infringement as well as gross negligence.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: Mutual indemnification is standard industry practice; we can agree to indemnify for customer-facing claims provided E.piphany indemnifies us for IP infringement and gross negligence.

redlines.originalText: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, OR DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, REVENUE, DATA OR USE, INCURRED BY THE OTHER PARTY OR ANY THIRD PARTY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION IN CONTRACT OR TORT, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES. IN NO EVENT SHALL E.PIPHANY'S LIABILITY HEREUNDER EXCEED THE SUM TOTAL OF PAYMENTS MADE BY HSNS UNDER THE INITIAL TERM OF THIS AGREEMENT.
redlines.proposedText: IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES. EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE CAPPED AT 1X THE TOTAL FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY HSNS IN THE PRECEDING 12-MONTH PERIOD, PROVIDED THAT THIS CAP SHALL NOT APPLY TO INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS OR BREACHES OF CONFIDENTIALITY.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany contends that its pricing structure reflects strict risk caps tied strictly to initial term payments for E.piphany only.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: One-sided liability caps leave HSNS exposed to uncapped liability while limiting E.piphany's exposure severely.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Liability caps must be symmetrical (1x trailing 12 months) with appropriate carve-outs for indemnification and confidentiality.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: A symmetrical liability cap tied to 12 months of fees aligns with enterprise standards; we can accept capping ordinary breach damages if indemnities remain outside the cap.

redlines.originalText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement of the parties, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Section 12.1.
redlines.proposedText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement of the parties. HSNS may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days prior written notice to E.piphany.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany claims multi-year commitments are required to amortize software development and operational setup.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Without termination for convenience, HSNS risk lock-in if commercial priorities shift or the software underperforms.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Enterprise buyers require flexibility to exit contracts via 30 days written notice for convenience.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We require a 30-day convenience termination clause to manage operational risk, but we can accept a fallback of 60 days notice if needed.

redlines.originalText: HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS pursuant to this Agreement, and hereby waives any and all moral rights that HSNS may retain in and to such customizations, enhancements, amendment and changes.
redlines.proposedText: HSNS retains ownership of all pre-existing IP, standalone custom deliverables, and HSNS data created under this Agreement. HSNS grants E.piphany a non-exclusive license to use feedback and core core modifications solely to maintain the Application.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany insists all enhancements derive from its core platform and must belong to E.piphany.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Forced assignment of custom enhancements forces HSNS to forfeit proprietary workflows and investments.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Custom deliverables developed for HSNS should belong to HSNS as work made for hire, while vendor retains underlying core platform IP.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: HSNS must own unique work product funded by HSNS, but we can grant E.piphany a perpetual license to platform-level software improvements.

obligations.requirement: HSNS shall meet with E.piphany on a quarterly basis to discuss non-binding forecasts and provide a non-binding, rolling six-month forecast report in advance.
obligations.breachConsequence: Material breach if not cured within thirty days of notice

obligations.requirement: All amounts due and owing by HSNS shall be paid within thirty days from the date of E.piphany's invoice.
obligations.breachConsequence: Late payment charge accrue at lesser of 1.5 percent per month or maximum rate allowed under law

obligations.requirement: HSNS shall discontinue use of the Application and certify in writing that all copies have been returned or destroyed.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners... Either party shall be solely responsible for, and shall indemnify and hold free and harmless the other party for, any and all claims, damages or lawsuits... arising from the tortious or grossly negligent acts of the indemnifying party's employees, agents or Contractors.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText:
(a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, and employees from and against any third-party claims, suits, or proceedings alleging that Customer's authorized use of the Services infringes any patent, copyright, trademark, or misappropriates any trade secret of a third party, and shall pay all settlements agreed to in writing or damages final-adjudicated by a court of competent jurisdiction.
(b) Customer Indemnification. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider against any third-party claims arising from Customer Data uploaded or transmitted in violation of Applicable Law or third-party proprietary rights.
(c) Procedure. The indemnified party shall provide prompt written notice of any claim, grant the indemnifying party sole control of defense and settlement (provided no settlement requires an admission of liability or payment of funds without prior consent), and provide reasonable assistance at the indemnifying party's expense.
deviations: Indemnity is largely one-sided in favor of Provider (E.piphany) under Section 10.2, with mutual indemnity limited to tortious or grossly negligent acts under Section 10.3.
Provider's IP infringement liability is capped as an exclusive remedy with option to modify, replace, or terminate and refund depreciated fees.
missingProtections: Comprehensive provider indemnity protecting Customer for third-party IP infringement claims with full defense and settlement coverage.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Negotiate a broad, balanced IP infringement indemnification obligation from Provider for Customer's authorized use of the application.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: 3.1, 3.4, 4.3, 6.2, 6.4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. All other rights and licenses granted herein will cease upon termination.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provisions which by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, indemnification, limitation of liability, payment of accrued fees, data return and deletion, and governing law, survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement.
deviations: Specifies survival by static section reference numbers rather than general category descriptions.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Verify that all key operational, confidentiality, liability, and payment section numbers are included in the explicit survival list in Section 13.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: THIS ALLOCATION TO WHICH THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED. THIS LIMITATION OF LIABILITY APPLIES NOTWITHSTANDING ANY FAILURE OF THE ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF THE EXCLUSIVE REMEDIES.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Limitation of Liability — 12-Month Trailing Aggregate Fee Cap with Balanced Super-Cap
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText:
(a) Consequential Damages Waiver. Except for breaches of Section 7 (Confidentiality) or indemnification obligations under Section 9, neither party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, special, incidental, punitive, or consequential damages, or loss of profits, revenue, or business opportunity, arising out of or related to this Agreement, regardless of the theory of liability.
(b) General Aggregate Cap. Except for excluded claims, each party's maximum aggregate liability arising under or related to this Agreement shall be limited to the total fees actually paid or payable by Customer to Provider in the twelve (12) month period preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
(c) Super-Cap for Data Protection Breaches. Liability arising from a material breach of Section 8 (Data Security and Privacy) shall be capped at three times (3x) the aggregate fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the breach.
deviations: Contract text in excerpt provides a disclaimer of remedies/essential purpose but lacks clear mutual 12-month trailing aggregate cap structure or data protection super-caps.
missingProtections: Clear mutual aggregate fee cap tied to 12 months of fees.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Incorporate a clear mutual aggregate cap equal to 12 months of paid fees and carve out data protection or confidentiality breaches into an appropriate super-cap.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto, including without limitation any customization, enhancement, amendment or change to the Application... For avoidance of doubt, modification to the Application to be owned by E.piphany shall not include pre-existing HSNS intellectual property or intellectual property developed by HSNS without reference to E.piphany Confidential Information. All data created by HSNS using the Outsourcing Application shall...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Rights — Customer Work Product Ownership & Non-Use of Customer Data for AI Training
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText:
(a) Work Product. All custom deliverables, reports, workflows, and specifications developed specifically for Customer under an applicable Statement of Work ('Work Product') shall constitute 'work made for hire' and belong exclusively to Customer upon payment.
(b) Customer Data & AI Model Boundaries. Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data. Provider shall not use Customer Data (including prompts, inputs, documents, and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, improve, or benchmark any generalized artificial intelligence, machine learning model, or large language model without Customer's express prior written consent.
(c) Feedback License. Any voluntary feedback provided regarding the Services may be used by Provider without restriction or obligation of confidentiality.
deviations: Provider retains ownership of all customizations, enhancements, and modifications made to the application.
Does not contain express prohibitions against using Customer Data for AI/ML training.
missingProtections: Customer ownership of custom deliverables developed under SOWs.
Explicit restrictions against training AI/ML models on Customer Data.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure Customer retains ownership of custom SOW deliverables and explicitly prohibit Provider from using Customer Data for AI or machine learning model training.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: ...rendered consistent with generally accepted industry standards for a period of ninety (90) days from performance of such services. 4.2 EXCLUSIVE REMEDIES... (i) in the case of a nonconforming Application, to correct the nonconforming Application... and, if E.piphany is unable to do so, HSNS shall be entitled to terminate the Application license and recover the fees paid... (iv) in the case of services... correction of defective work...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Warranties — Performance Warranty with Re-Performance Remedy
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: The Provider warrants that (a) the Services will perform materially in accordance with the Documentation, (b) Services will be performed in a professional manner consistent with industry standards, and (c) it will not knowingly introduce malicious code. If a warranty is breached and reported within ninety (90) days, the Provider shall re-perform or correct the non-conformity; if it cannot do so within thirty (30) days, the Customer may terminate the affected Services and receive a refund of prepaid fees for them.
deviations: Contract remedies restrict claims to exclusive remedies of correction or license termination without explicit malicious code representation in excerpt.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add explicit warranties that the software contains no malicious code or backdoors, alongside existing 90-day performance and professional service warranties.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: For avoidance of doubt, modification to the Application to be owned by E.piphany shall not include pre-existing HSNS intellectual property or intellectual property developed by HSNS without reference to E.piphany Confidential Information.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Ownership — Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment. To the extent any Provider pre-existing materials are embedded in a deliverable, the Provider grants the Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use them as part of that deliverable.
deviations: Contract preserves Customer's pre-existing IP, but assigns all newly created modifications and enhancements to the application to Provider.
missingProtections: Perpetual embedded license for Customer in deliverables containing Provider pre-existing IP.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Clarify that while pre-existing IP remains with its original owner, Customer receives a perpetual, royalty-free license to any embedded Provider IP in deliverables.

rules.evidence: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners... arising out of or resulting from (i) HSNS's providing or failure to provide Outsourcing Services
rules.explanation: The indemnity structure is heavily biased, forcing Customer to provide broad indemnification while Vendor limits its IP indemnification to US IP and excludes liabilities for combinations or modifications.
rules.recommendation: Negotiate a symmetrical indemnification clause where Vendor unconditionally indemnifies Customer against third-party IP infringement, gross negligence, and security breaches, while removing broad customer indemnity obligations.

rules.evidence: IN NO EVENT SHALL E.PIPHANY'S LIABILITY HEREUNDER EXCEED THE SUM TOTAL OF PAYMENTS MADE BY HSNS UNDER THE INITIAL TERM OF THIS AGREEMENT.
rules.explanation: The liability cap applies strictly to E.piphany while excluding direct liabilities, and fails to provide standard uncapped exceptions for indemnity, confidentiality, or data breaches.
rules.recommendation: Make the aggregate liability cap symmetrical for both parties capped at 12 months of fees, and explicitly exclude IP infringement, confidentiality breaches, and gross negligence from the liability cap.

rules.evidence: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B... either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party becomes insolvent... or fails to cure a material breach
rules.explanation: The contract only permits termination for cause or insolvency, lacking a provision for Customer to terminate for convenience with 30 days written notice.
rules.recommendation: Add a clause granting Customer the right to terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time upon 30 days prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid unearned fees.

rules.evidence: HSNS acknowledges and agrees that any and all Deliverables shall be and remain the property of E.piphany.
rules.explanation: Vendor retains ownership over all deliverables created under the agreement, granting Customer only a non-exclusive license.
rules.recommendation: Amend the agreement to stipulate that custom deliverables developed specifically for Customer are owned by Customer as 'Work Made for Hire', or at minimum obtain an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide license.

rules.explanation: The provided contract excerpts contain no security standards or data breach notification timeframe.
rules.recommendation: Insert a data security provision requiring Vendor to adhere to standard security frameworks and notify Customer within 24 hours of any suspected or actual data breach.

rules.evidence: Each Deliverable shall be deemed accepted upon the earlier of: (i) receipt of written notice of acceptance from HSNS, or (ii) ten (10) days after delivery of such Deliverable ("Acceptance Period")
rules.explanation: Deliverables are automatically deemed accepted after 10 days if not formally rejected, which is overly restrictive compared to Net 45 and standard acceptance workflow.
rules.recommendation: Remove automatic standard deemed acceptance within 10 days, extend acceptance evaluation periods, and link payment terms to Net 45 days after verified written acceptance.

opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will maintain that its software pricing is strictly risk-allocated and based on limiting its maximum exposure to fees collected during the initial term.

opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will claim that multi-year commitment terms are required to amortize software development and operational setup fees.
